|number = 8191

'''8191''' ('''eight thousand one hundred [and] ninety-one''') is the [[natural number]] following 8190, and preceding [[8192]]. It is also known as M(13).{{efn|1=M(13) is the mathematical notation for the 13th Mersenne prime (''M<sub>p</sub>'' = 2''<sup>p</sup>'' − 1) where the exponent number is 13.}}

== In mathematics ==
8191 is an [[odd number]] and the 1028th [[prime number]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Vanovschi |first=Vitalii |title=Properties of the number 8191 |url=http://www.numberempire.com:80/8191 |access-date=2026-08-23 |website=www.numberempire.com |language=en}}</ref> It is also a [[Jacobsthal-Lucas number]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A014551|Jacobsthal-Lucas numbers}}</ref> It is a [[palindrome]] and [[repdigit]] in [[base 2]], which has 13 repeated digits of the number [[one]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Number 8191 - Properties & Facts {{!}} NumberWorld |url=https://numberworld.info/8191 |access-date=2026-08-23 |website=numberworld.info |language=en}}</ref>

=== Mersenne prime ===
It is most notable for being a [[Mersenne prime]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web |first=Erich |last=Friedman |title=What's Special About This Number?|url=https://erich-friedman.github.io/numbers.html |access-date=2026-08-23}}</ref> Since it is a Mersenne prime, it can be expressed as 2<sup>13</sup> − 1.<ref>{{cite book |last1 = Roggero |first1 = Pier Francesco |last2 = Nardelli |first2 = Michele |last3 = Di Noto |first3 = Francesco |title = Study on the Perfect Numbers and Mersenne's Prime with New Developments: Possible Mathematical Connections with Some Sectors of String Theory |date = 2012-12-14 |url = https://d1wqtxts1xzle7.cloudfront.net/64913789/Study_on_the_perfect_numbers_and_Mersenne_b-libre.pdf 
| access-date = 2026-08-23 
}}</ref> And since the [[exponent]] number is prime, it is considered one.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=MacDougall |first=Jim |date=March 2003 |title=Mersenne composites and cyclotomic primes |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematical-gazette/article/abs/mersenne-composites-and-cyclotomic-primes/6CDE763C37E34061D4E410B2451E981B |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |language=en |volume=87 |issue=508 |pages=71–75 |doi=10.1017/S0025557200172122 |issn=0025-5572}}</ref><ref>{{cite OEIS|A000668|Mersenne primes}}</ref> It was discovered anonymously before 1461.<ref>{{Cite web |title=List of known Mersenne prime numbers - PrimeNet |url=https://www.mersenne.org/primes/ |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=www.mersenne.org}}</ref>
